evidence.text:
Title: Phase Diagram of the Ashkin-Teller Model
Abstract: The Ashkin-Teller model is a pair of interacting Ising models and has two parameters: J is a coupling constant in the Ising models and U describes the strength of the interaction between them. In the ferromagnetic case J,U>0 on the square lattice, we establish a complete phase diagram conjectured in physics in 1970s (by Kadanoff and Wegner, Wu and Lin, Baxter and others): when J<U, the transitions for the Ising spins and their products occur at two distinct curves that are dual to each other; when J\geq U, both transitions occur at the self-dual curve. All transitions are shown to be sharp using the OSSS inequality. We use a finite-criterion argument and continuity to extend the result of Peled and the third author \cite{GlaPel19} from a self-dual point to its neighborhood. Our proofs go through the random-cluster representation of the Ashkin-Teller model introduced by Chayes-Machta and Pfister-Velenik and we rely on couplings to FK-percolation.

Title: On critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model
Abstract: The critical properties of the Ashkin-Teller model in the special case where two pair energies are the same are shown to be the same as those of the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit as a consequence of scaling hypothesis.

gold.abstract: The Ashkin-Teller model can be represented by a pair $(τ,τ')$ of Ising spin configurations with coupling constants $J$ and $J'$ for each, and $U$ for their product. We study this representation on the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq 2$. We confirm the presence of a partial antiferromagnetic phase in the isotropic case ($J=J'$) when $-U>0$ is sufficiently large and $J=J'>0$ is sufficiently small, by means of a graphical representation. In this phase, $τ$ is disordered, admitting exponential decay of correlations, while the product $ττ'$ is antiferromagnetically ordered, which is to say that correlations are bounded away from zero but alternate in sign. No correlation inequalities are available in this part of the phase diagram. In the planar case $d=2$, we construct a coupling with the six-vertex model and show, in analogy to the first result, that the corresponding height function is localised, although with antiferromagnetically ordered heights on one class of vertices of the graph.   We then return to $d\geq 2$ and consider a part of the phase diagram where $U<0$ but where correlation inequalities still apply. Using the OSSS inequality, we proceed to establish a subcritical sharpness statement along suitable curves covering this part, circumventing the difficulty of the lack of general monotonicity properties in the parameters. We then address the isotropic case and provide indications of monotonicity.

J = J′ > 0 is sufficiently small, by means of a graphical representation.
gold.title: On antiferromagnetic regimes in the Ashkin-Teller model

These are your colleagues' latest proposals:

--- Researcher B ---
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS  
- Paper B provides a rigorous ferromagnetic square-lattice Ashkin-Teller phase diagram: sharp transitions, dual curves for J<U, self-dual curve for J≥U, random-cluster representation, and FK-percolation couplings.  
- Paper C claims that when two pair energies coincide, the Ashkin-Teller critical properties match the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit via scaling hypothesis.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM  
Paper C’s scaling claim lacks a concrete microscopic test; Paper B supplies the random-cluster/FK representation and a proven critical line. If Paper C’s correspondence holds near the equal-coupling case—candidate J=U on Paper B’s self-dual curve—then FK connectivity observables and spin observables along that curve should follow eight-vertex weak-coupling finite-size scaling. Paper B’s sharpness result guarantees a well-defined critical domain; Paper C’s hypothesis supplies the predicted universality class.

RESEARCH DESIGN  
Simulate the Ashkin-Teller random-cluster model on L×L square lattices along Paper B’s self-dual curve and nearby dual curves. Measure magnetization, product-spin, and FK cluster-size moments; compute correlation-length ratios, Binder cumulants, and exponent estimates using finite-size scaling. Validate by testing whether these exponent pairs and universal amplitude ratios match eight-vertex weak-coupling predictions from Paper C. Use the FK coupling to check internal consistency between cluster and spin observables. Missing cross-paper knowledge: Paper C does not explicitly identify its “two equal pair energies” with Paper B’s J,U; we treat J=U as the primary candidate and vary nearby as a robustness check.

WORKING ABSTRACT  
We propose a finite-size-scaling test of the Ashkin-Teller/eight-vertex correspondence. Using Paper B’s rigorous random-cluster representation and phase diagram, we simulate along the self-dual equal-coupling line, extract FK and spin critical exponents, and test whether they match eight-vertex weak-coupling predictions. This would turn Paper C’s scaling-hypothesis claim into an explicit, validated universality statement.

FINAL IDEA: Use the rigorous random-cluster/FK phase diagram of the Ashkin-Teller model as a numerical laboratory to test whether its equal-coupling self-dual critical line obeys eight-vertex weak-coupling finite-size scaling.

--- Researcher C ---
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper B supplies a rigorous, complete ferromagnetic phase diagram for the square-lattice Ashkin-Teller model: for J<U two dual transition curves, for J≥U a single self-dual transition. It proves sharpness via OSSS, using the Chayes-Machta/Pfister-Velenik random-cluster representation and couplings to FK-percolation, plus continuity from a self-dual point.
- Paper C claims that, when two pair energies are equal—interpretable as the self-dual case J=U—the Ashkin-Teller critical properties coincide with those of the eight-vertex model in the weak-coupling limit, as a consequence of the scaling hypothesis.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Use Paper B’s random-cluster/FK coupling along the J=U self-dual curve to give a microscopic, geometric route to Paper C’s scaling identification. The AT random-cluster representation generates loop ensembles whose boundaries are FK-percolation-like. The proposal hypothesizes that these loop ensembles converge, on the self-dual line, to the weak-coupling eight-vertex loop model. Thus Paper C’s scaling-hypothesis equivalence becomes operationally testable through Paper B’s sharp-transition geometry rather than assumed scaling.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Simulate the AT random-cluster representation on finite square lattices at J=U across U values, using Chayes-Machta updates. Measure: wrapping probabilities, two-point connection probabilities, cluster-size moments, and loop-boundary fractal dimension. Perform finite-size scaling and compare measured critical exponents with weak-coupling eight-vertex exponent values; universality collapse is the test of Paper C’s claim. Validate the simulation by recovering Paper B’s self-dual transition location. Missing cross-paper knowledge: Paper C does not give explicit exponent values or an operator dictionary; Paper B does not identify scaling limits, so the AT random-cluster observable-to-eight-vertex operator mapping must be supplied independently.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We test the scaling-hypothesis equivalence between the self-dual Ashkin-Teller model and the weak-coupling eight-vertex model by studying loop ensembles from the rigorous AT random-cluster/FK couplings. Finite-size scaling of random-cluster observables along J=U provides a quantitative universality check that connects the proven phase diagram to conjectured eight-vertex critical behavior.

FINAL IDEA: Use the rigorous random-cluster/FK couplings of the Ashkin-Teller phase diagram to turn the scaling-hypothesis equivalence between the self-dual Ashkin-Teller and weak-coupling eight-vertex models into a quantitative, testable loop-ensemble correspondence.
